info.bio: Nació el 1 de abril de 1948 en St. James, Jamaica. Su carrera se inició tocando ska en varias agrupaciones de la isla. Pero no fue sino hasta 1967 cuando compuso canciones para la película de Perry Henzell 'The Harder They Come' que obtuvo reconocimiento y trascendencia entre los medios internacionales, lo que ayudó a que el disco del film mencionado fuera considerado uno de los álbumes más vendidos en la historia del reggae. scenes.name: Reggae y dub
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El reggae se populariza en el Reino Unido con Prince Buster y Desmond Dekker; Jimmy Cliff lo casa con el «paz y amor» hippy y los Maytals le dan nombre. Los sound systems de los guetos convierten a los «selectors» en los verdaderos animadores: el «toasting» sobre los discos será tan importante como la música. Bob Marley y los Wailers lo llevan a Occidente; Burning Spear firma quizá su cima artística (Marcus Garvey). Los ingenieros remezclan las caras B quitando las voces: King Tubby inventa el dub usando la mesa de mezclas como un instrumento, y Lee Perry (Super Ape) y Augustus Pablo fijan el canon.

podcast.title: Role in The Harder They Come (1972)
podcast.body: Jimmy Cliff starred as Ivan, a musician who is exploited by the music industry, receiving only $20 for a song he wrote. This exploitation leads him to a life of crime in Kingston, Jamaica. He described the film as a "landmark movie" because of its realism, with none of the actors being professionals. "The musician Jimmy Clip played Ivan, a musician who has taken advantage of by the music industry and only gets $20 for a song that he wrote."

podcast.title: Reggae's Natural Fit (1976)
podcast.body: In 1976, Jimmy Cliff articulated his view that reggae was the inherent music of the 70s, perceiving it as the most complete contemporary genre that resonated with the prevailing lifestyle aspirations of the era. "Jimmy Cliff said in 1976 that reggae is the natural music of the 70s. It is the most complete contemporary form of music that fits with the lifestyle that people are trying to live."

podcast.title: Jimmy Cliff Death (2025) – Seizure and Pneumonia at 81, Predecessor to Bob Marley
podcast.body: Jimmy Cliff, the pioneering reggae artist and Jamaican national hero who predated Bob Marley in bringing reggae to global audiences, died at age 81 of a seizure and pneumonia. "The great pioneer of reggae, predecessor of Bob Marley in the global rise of the genre."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Authenticity of The Harder They Come
podcast.body: Jimmy Cliff, reflecting 50 years later, stated that "The Harder They Come" was a landmark movie due to its authentic portrayal of life, with non-professional actors and a story that resonated with anyone from the country looking to make a life in the city. "it was such a landmark movie because it was very real. None of us were professional actors. Clip says. The story is the story of any one of us who was born in the country or coming from the country."

podcast.title: Collaborated with Millie Small
podcast.body: Jimmy Cliff was one of several artists with whom Millie Small was teamed in attempts to revive her chart success after "My Boy Lollipop." "She recorded with Jimmy Cliff."
